note: Flow Row PATTERN LIBRARY (prompts/TEAMWORK_FRAMEWORK.md §26). Every row is a SAMPLE: referenced rows live in the named flows*.json files and are already witnessed; 'inline' rows are labelled SAMPLE and compile-checked here. A pattern with no witnessed behaviour is not in this file.

patterns.name: A branch sells, head office answers with stock
patterns.want: My branch records sales and sends them to head office at the end of the day. Head office checks stock and sends a replenishment back.
adjust: table and carries: the records that travel and the columns that matter
group: what makes one record unique, so a resend is recognised
process: the name of the process head office runs when the sale arrives

patterns.name: A price list pushed to one branch
patterns.want: Head office publishes a price list; each branch picks it up when it next connects, once a day.
adjust: role: which devices receive it
guard: daily = ask at most once a day; once = ask only until you have a value

patterns.name: A public value anyone may fetch
patterns.want: A value everyone is allowed to read, such as today's gold price or the list of cashiers, fetched once a day.
adjust: audience public: no role is needed to read it
guard once: for a value that never changes (the roster)

patterns.name: A code that carries value (loyalty points, store credit)
patterns.want: The shop issues a signed code worth points; the customer's phone applies it once; head office checks the books at the end.
adjust: authorityRole: who may issue the code
holderRole: who applies it
account: what the balance is called

patterns.name: A customer pays, the lender confirms
patterns.want: A borrower's payment slip goes up to the lender; the lender applies it and sends a confirmation back to that borrower.
adjust: role: BORROWER here is a label, use your own role
process: the named process that applies a payment

patterns.name: A team shares the records of a dictionary table
patterns.want: Everyone on the team can create and change business partners, and everyone ends up with the same list.
adjust: table and carries: carry every mandatory column or the receiver cannot build the record
dir BOTH needs audience space; they come as a pair

patterns.name: A team shares records that are not in the dictionary
patterns.want: My application has its own kind of record (a drawn element) that the dictionary does not know. The team should still share it, and only the kinds I list.
adjust: virtualTable and its columns: describe the record yourself, because there is no dictionary to read
values: the list of allowed kinds; adding a kind later is adding one value, no code

patterns.name: A table that stays on its own station
patterns.want: Numbering counters, recent-item lists and session logs belong to one station. Say so, so nobody shares them by mistake.
adjust: table: any table that must never leave its station
a table with no row at all is also local; a LOCAL row just makes the decision visible

patterns.name: Another table, same shape, no code
patterns.want: I already have a flow for order lines. I want invoice lines to behave the same way.
adjust: copy a row, change name and table; leave carries out to get a PROPOSAL, then trim it
a proposal is a starting point, never the plan

mistakes.title: A column name with a typo
mistakes.fix: Use the exact dictionary column name (QtyEntered).

mistakes.title: A table that does not exist
mistakes.fix: Check the table name in the dictionary.

mistakes.title: A required setting left out
mistakes.fix: Say what makes one record unique (the group).

mistakes.title: Both ways, but not as a team
mistakes.say: FACT dir BOTH needs audience space
mistakes.fix: Both-ways flows are for a team: set audience to space.

mistakes.title: A team flow that only goes one way
mistakes.say: FACT audience space needs dir BOTH
mistakes.fix: A team shares both ways: set dir to BOTH.

mistakes.title: A kind of movement that is not registered
mistakes.fix: Use FACT, SEED, RULE, INSTRUMENT or LOCAL, or register a new treatment.

mistakes.title: A made-up kind of column
mistakes.say: V1 bim_element: pos_x has unknown class MONEY
mistakes.fix: Use KEY, REF, MEASURE, DATE, FLAG, CODE, TEXT or OTHER.

mistakes.title: The same column declared twice
mistakes.fix: Each column once (names are not case-sensitive).

mistakes.title: Sending a column the system computes
mistakes.fix: Send what a person types; let the receiver compute the rest.

mistakes.title: A mandatory column left out
mistakes.fix: Carry it, or be sure the receiver can supply it.

mistakes.title: A rule with nothing to send
mistakes.fix: Name the flow the rule sends.

mistakes.title: A rule that names a flow that does not exist
mistakes.say: RULE emits names a row that does not exist: F9 replenishment-typo
mistakes.fix: Use the exact name of the row the rule should send.
